subject: math
title: Grade 7 Circles: Circumference and Area
seo_title: Grade 7 Circles Worksheets: Circumference and Area, Free Math with Answer Key (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Demonstrate an understanding of the inter-relationships between the radius, diameter, and area of a circle, and use the relationships to develop the formula for the area of a circle, and solve related problems
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 math worksheets on circles for the Ontario curriculum: radius and diameter, circumference C = πd = 2πr, area A = πr² and finding the radius or diameter from the circumference, with wheel, table, garden and hockey rink problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Circumference C = πd = 2πr. Area A = πr². Use π ≈ 3.14.
key_sub: The diameter is 2 radii, so halve d before you use A = πr². C = πr is missing the 2. C is a length (cm); A is in square units (cm²).
body_html:
Parts of a circle

The centre is the middle point. A radius (r) joins the centre to the edge. A diameter (d) goes all the way across through the centre. The circumference (C) is the distance around the circle: its perimeter.

Circumference: C = πd = 2πr

Measure any circle: C ÷ d is always the same number. It is called π (pi). π = 3.14159…, and in these worksheets we use π ≈ 3.14. So the circumference is a little more than 3 diameters, or a little more than 6 radii.

Example 1

A bike wheel has a diameter of 70 cm. How far does it roll in one turn?

C = πd ≈ 3.14 × 70 = 219.8

Answer: 219.8 cm

Example 2

A circle has a radius of 4 m. Find its circumference.

d = 2 × 4 = 8 m. C = πd ≈ 3.14 × 8 = 25.12

Answer: 25.12 m

Area: A = πr²

Square the radius, then multiply by π. The circle covers about 3.14 squares of side r. Area is in square units, such as cm² or m².

Example 3

A round table has a diameter of 1.6 m. Find the area of its top.

r = 1.6 ÷ 2 = 0.8 m. r² = 0.64. A = πr² ≈ 3.14 × 0.64 = 2.0096

Answer: about 2.01 m²

Working backwards

If you know the circumference, divide by π to get the diameter: d = C ÷ π. Then halve it for the radius, or divide C by 2π (about 6.28) in one step.

Example 4

A tree trunk is 2.198 m around. Find its radius.

d = C ÷ π ≈ 2.198 ÷ 3.14 = 0.7 m. r = 0.7 ÷ 2 = 0.35

Answer: 0.35 m

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the diameter in A = πr²Halve d first: r = d ÷ 2
C = πrC = 2πr (or C = πd)
Squaring π: (3.14 × 5)²Square only r: 3.14 × 5²
Mixing up C and AC is a length (m); A is an area (m²)
Multiplying C by π to find dDivide: d = C ÷ π

faq.q: When do Ontario students learn the area of a circle?
faq.a: In Grade 7. The Ontario math curriculum (Spatial Sense, E2.3 and E2.5) has students find the circumference with C = πd and develop and use A = πr².

faq.q: What is the difference between circumference and area?
faq.a: Circumference is the distance around a circle, measured in units like cm or m. Area is the space inside it, measured in square units like cm² or m².

faq.q: What value of π should Grade 7 students use?
faq.a: Most Grade 7 work uses π ≈ 3.14 or the π key on a calculator. These worksheets use 3.14, so every answer can be checked by hand.

faq.q: How do you find the radius if you know the circumference?
faq.a: Divide the circumference by π to get the diameter, then halve it. For example, C = 31.4 cm gives d = 31.4 ÷ 3.14 = 10 cm and r = 5 cm.

items.q: The red segment joins the centre to the edge. What is it called?
items.e: A segment from the centre to the edge is a radius.

items.q: What is the red segment called?
items.e: It crosses the whole circle and passes through the centre, so it is a diameter.

items.q: The red line goes all the way around the circle. What is it called?
items.e: The distance around a circle is its circumference: the perimeter of the circle.

items.q: The red point is the same distance from every point on the edge. What is it called?
items.e: The middle point, the same distance from every point on the edge, is the centre.

items.q: A diameter of a circle is always 2 times as long as…
items.e: A diameter is two radii end to end, so d = 2r. It is 2 times as long as a radius.

items.q: The number π is the ratio of which two measures of a circle?
items.e: For every circle, C ÷ d is the same number, π ≈ 3.14. So π is circumference to diameter. C ÷ r is 2π and d ÷ r is 2.

items.q: About how many radii fit around the circumference of a circle?
items.e: C = 2πr ≈ 6.28 × r, so a little more than 6 radii fit around. A little more than 3 is the number of diameters.

items.q: A circle has a diameter of 12 cm. Which is the shortest?
items.e: r = 6 cm, d = 12 cm and C ≈ 3.14 × 12 = 37.68 cm. The radius is the shortest.

items.q: Priya opens her compass to 6 cm and draws a circle. What is the diameter of the circle?
items.e: The compass opening is the radius: r = 6 cm. d = 2 × 6 = 12 cm.

items.q: All the radii of one circle are…
items.e: Every point on the circle is the same distance from the centre, so all radii are the same length.

items.q: Which formula gives the circumference of a circle with diameter d?
items.e: The circumference is π times the diameter: C = πd. πr² is the area.

items.q: Which formula gives the circumference of a circle with radius r?
items.e: d = 2r, so C = πd = π × 2r = 2πr. C = πr forgets the 2 and gives half the answer.

items.q: Find the circumference. Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: C = πd ≈ 3.14 × 22 = 69.08 cm. Do not double it: 2π goes with the radius, not the diameter.

Circle A has a diameter of 14 cm. Circle B has a radius of 8 cm. Which has the longer circumference?
items.e: Circle B has d = 2 × 8 = 16 cm, which is more than 14 cm. C ≈ 3.14 × 14 = 43.96 cm for A and 3.14 × 16 = 50.24 cm for B. Circle B.

items.q: The radius of a circle triples from 2 cm to 6 cm. What happens to the circumference?
items.e: C = 2πr: 2 × 3.14 × 2 = 12.56 cm and 2 × 3.14 × 6 = 37.68 cm. 37.68 ÷ 12.56 = 3, so the circumference triples.

items.q: Which formula gives the area of a circle?
items.e: A = πr²: square the radius, then multiply by π. πd² uses the diameter and gives 4 times too much.

items.q: A circle has a diameter of 8 m. In which unit is its area measured?
items.e: Area counts squares, so it is in square units of the same length unit: m². The circumference is a length, in m.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 6 cm. Find its area. Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: A = πr² ≈ 3.14 × 6 × 6 = 3.14 × 36 = 113.04 cm². Square the radius, not π.

sets.title: Finding r or d from the circumference

items.q: You know the circumference of a circle. How do you find its diameter?
items.e: C = πd, so d = C ÷ π. Divide C by π (about 3.14).

items.q: You know the circumference of a circle. How do you find its radius?
items.e: C = 2πr, so r = C ÷ 2π. Divide C by 2π (about 6.28). Dividing by π gives the diameter.

sets.title: Word problems: wheels, tables, gardens and rinks

items.q: Noah’s bike wheel has a diameter of 62 cm. How far does the bike move in one full turn of the wheel? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: One turn rolls out the circumference. C = πd ≈ 3.14 × 62 = 194.68 cm.

items.q: Noah’s wheel moves 194.68 cm in one turn. How many metres does the bike move in 500 turns?
Ethan rides 2 km on the Martin Goodman Trail in Toronto. His wheels have a diameter of 50 cm. About how many full turns does each wheel make? (2 km = 200 000 cm) Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: C = πd ≈ 3.14 × 50 = 157 cm. 200 000 ÷ 157 ≈ 1273.9, so about 1274 turns. Dividing by 50 forgets π.

items.q: A round table in the school library is 1.5 m across. What is the area of the tabletop, to the nearest hundredth? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: 1.5 m across is the diameter, so r = 0.75 m. r² = 0.5625. A = πr² ≈ 3.14 × 0.5625 = 1.76625 ≈ 1.77 m².

items.q: Olivia glues ribbon around the edge of the same round table, 1.5 m across. How much ribbon does she need, to the nearest tenth of a metre? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: The edge is the circumference. C = πd ≈ 3.14 × 1.5 = 4.71 ≈ 4.7 m.

items.q: A circular garden at a school in Hamilton has a radius of 2.5 m. How long is a fence that goes all the way around it? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: The fence is the circumference. d = 5 m, so C = πd ≈ 3.14 × 5 = 15.7 m.

items.q: The same circular garden has a radius of 2.5 m. What area does it cover, to the nearest hundredth? Use π ≈ 3.14.
Aiden puts a fence around a circular garden with a radius of 3 m. The fencing costs $15 per metre. How much does the fencing cost? Use π ≈ 3.14.
A circular flower bed has a diameter of 6 m. One bag of mulch covers 3 m². How many bags does Amira need to cover the whole bed? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: r = 3 m. A = πr² ≈ 3.14 × 9 = 28.26 m². 28.26 ÷ 3 = 9.42, so 9 bags are not quite enough. She needs 10 bags.

items.q: Owen wraps a rope around a white pine trunk in Algonquin Park. The rope measures 2.826 m. What is the diameter of the trunk? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: The rope measures the circumference. d = C ÷ π ≈ 2.826 ÷ 3.14 = 0.9 m.

items.q: A lawn sprinkler waters a circle with a radius of 6 m. What area of grass does it water? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: A = πr² ≈ 3.14 × 36 = 113.04 m². 37.68 is the circumference, not the area.

items.q: A round trampoline has a diameter of 4.2 m. A safety net goes all the way around the edge. How long is the net, to the nearest tenth of a metre? Use π ≈ 3.14.
Which gives more pizza: one round pizza 36 cm across, or two round pizzas 24 cm across? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: 36 cm pizza: r = 18, A ≈ 3.14 × 324 = 1017.36 cm². Two 24 cm pizzas: r = 12, A ≈ 2 × 452.16 = 904.32 cm². So one 36 cm pizza gives more, even though 24 + 24 > 36.

items.q: A face-off circle on the ice at an arena in Sudbury has a radius of 4.5 m. How long is the painted red line around it? Use π ≈ 3.14.
The face-off circle has a radius of 4.5 m. What area of ice is inside it, to the nearest tenth? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: r² = 4.5 × 4.5 = 20.25. A = πr² ≈ 3.14 × 20.25 = 63.585 ≈ 63.6 m². Using d = 9 m in πr² gives 254.3 m², 4 times too much.

items.q: A circular path around a pond in an Ottawa park has a radius of 40 m. Chloe walks around it 4 times. How far does she walk? Use π ≈ 3.14.
The edge of a round tree stump at the cottage measures 1.884 m around. What is the radius of the stump? Use π ≈ 3.14.
Maya’s hand drum has a round top 50 cm across. What is the area of the drum’s top? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: 50 cm across is the diameter, so r = 25 cm. A = πr² ≈ 3.14 × 625 = 1962.5 cm².

items.q: Which is longer: the circumference of a circle with a diameter of 12 cm, or the perimeter of a square with 9 cm sides? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: Circle: C ≈ 3.14 × 12 = 37.68 cm. Square: P = 4 × 9 = 36 cm. The circle’s circumference is longer by 1.68 cm.

items.q: A Ferris wheel at the Canadian National Exhibition (CNE) in Toronto has a diameter of 24 m. How far does a seat travel in one full turn? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: The seat travels the circumference. C = πd ≈ 3.14 × 24 = 75.36 m.
